div.l: He was not to synfull men . dispitous .
Ne of his speche . daungerous ne digne .
But in his speche . discreet ⁊and benygne .
To drawen folke to heuyn . bi fairnes .
Bi good ensample . this was his besynes .
But yf it were . ony persone obstynate .
What so he were . of lowe or high estate .
Hym wolde he snybbe . scharpely for the nones .
A better preest I trowe . nowher non ys .
He wayted after . no pompe ne reuerens .
Ne makid hym . a spiced consciens .
But cristes lore . ⁊and his apostels twelue .
He taught . but first he vsid it hym selue .
With hym ther was a ploughman . was his brother .
That had lad of donge . full many a /fother .
And a trewe swynker . ⁊and a good was he .
Lyuyng in pees . ⁊and ꝑperfite charite .
God loued he best . with all his herte .
At all tymes . though hym gamed or smerte .
And than his neyghbore . right as hym selue .
He wolde þressche . ⁊and ther to dike ⁊and delue .
For cristes sake . for euery poor wight .
With oute hire . yf it lay in his myght .
His tithes paied he . full faire ⁊and well .
Bothe of his propre swynke . ⁊and his catell .
In a tabbarde . he rode vp on a mere .
Ther / was also . a Reue ⁊and a Millere .
A sompnorur . ⁊and a Perdoner also .
A manciple ⁊and my self . ther / were no moo .
The myllere was a stout carle . for the nones .
Full bigge he was . of brawne ⁊and eke of bones .
That preued well . for ouer all ther he cam .
At wrastlyng / . he wolde haue a weye the ram .
He was schort schuldred . a thicke knarre .
Ther ne was no dore . that he ne wolde heue of barre .
Or breke it at a rennyng . with his heed .
His beerd as any sowe . or fox was reed .
And ther / to brood . as though it were a spade .
Vp on the cop . right of his nose he hade .
A werte . ⁊and ther on stood . a tufte of heres .
Reed as the bristelles . of a sowes eres .
His nose thrilles . blake were ⁊and wide .
A swerde ⁊and a bokeler / . bar he bi his side .
His mouthe was as gret . as a gret furneis .
He was a iangeler . ⁊and a goliardeis .
And that was moost of synne . ⁊and of harlotries .
Well couthe he stele corn . ⁊and tollen thries . /
